Hi Lisa / Tom,

Thanks again for the time today. Per our discussion I put together a concise mutual action plan (MAP) focused on the performance evaluation you requested for the embeddings + reranker flow. The goal is to validate that Redwood can meet SearchCorp's latency and concurrency targets for the pilot (and understand scaling costs).

High-level MAP items (first pass):
- 2026-06-10 to 2026-06-14: Share test plan & configs; agree on workload (query mix, pair counts).
- 2026-06-15 to 2026-06-16: Run perf tests on Redwood Dedicated and Hosted variants; collect raw logs/metrics.
- 2026-06-17: Deliver consolidated perf report (latency/throughput/TTFT, p50/p95/p99, concurrency curves).
- 2026-06-18: Decision call (pilot go/no-go) and discuss procurement timeline.

Target success criteria (examples to confirm):
- Embeddings endpoint: p95 latency < 50ms at sustained 500 qps (batching allowed).
- Reranker endpoint (embed pairs -> score): end-to-end TTFT p95 < 200ms at 100 concurrent requests; throughput >= 300 pairs/sec for typical pair batch sizes.

Attached: embed_rerank_test_plan_20260610.pdf with test harness, models, and measurement definitions.

Please confirm these targets and the MAP dates; we can update before running tests.

Best,
Monica

Subject: Re: SearchCorp MAP: performance plan & benchmarks — embeddings + reranker

Monica / Lisa / Neha — attaching the raw test results and a short summary. We ran the matrix across: Hosted (prod-like) and Dedicated (g5.2xlarge pool, 2 x A10G equiv) using our standard perf harness (locust + custom token-level tracing). Models used: embed-small-1536 (q8), rerank-xlarge (q8-sliced). Test artifacts attached: 20260616_searchcorp_map_perf_results.csv and plots in the Drive link.

Summary of key outcomes (short):
- Embeddings (short inputs, 5-20 tokens): sustained throughput 2,400 qps (batch size 64), p50 5.8ms, p95 38ms, p99 68ms. Hosted and Dedicated configs both passed SearchCorp's 500 qps target with p95 < 50ms.
- Embeddings (long inputs, 200-512 tokens): throughput drops to ~320 qps (batch size 8), p95 210ms on Hosted, 175ms on Dedicated (quantization helps but long token windows show expected increases).
- Reranker (candidate set 10): end-to-end TTFT p95 = 130ms at 100 concurrency on Dedicated (batching=16 for internal scoring ops); throughput ~360 pairs/sec. Hosted showed p95 = 180ms at 100 concurrency.
- Reranker (candidate set 25): at 100 concurrency p95 ~260ms on Hosted (miss SLA), ~210ms on Dedicated (marginal). At 200 concurrency we see tail latency growth and significant CPU contended signals on the host.

Observed failure modes and notes:
- >150 concurrency without sharding leads to queueing in the scorer and p99 spikes.
- Long-input embeddings are the dominant cost driver if you pass full-context long queries through the same endpoint; recommend separate sizing or offload long-form embeddings to a different pool.
- Caching prefixes (client-side or prefix KV cache) reduces reranker per-query work ~25% in our tests for search flows with overlapping prefixes.

Recommended mitigations for pilot:
1) Target Dedicated pool for the pilot with 2x workers for reranker to handle 100-200 concurrency headroom.
2) Use a separate instance group for long-form embeddings; set lower batch sizes and advertise lower throughput SLO.
3) Enable prefix KV caching for reranker and tune batching to target 10-16 candidates per internal scoring batch.
4) For immediate procurement numbers: estimated cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated at pilot scale ~30% in favor of Dedicated for unit token costs (but requires reservation). Detailed cost table in attachment.

I'll highlight a few numbers directly from the CSV:
- embeddings_short_p95_dedicated_ms = 38
- embeddings_long_p95_dedicated_ms = 175
- rerank_10_p95_dedicated_ms = 130
- rerank_25_p95_dedicated_ms = 210
- rerank_throughput_pairs_per_sec_dedicated = 360

Let us know if you want a follow-up run with sharded reranker workers (we can provision + run in ~24hrs).

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Lisa / Tom — sharing an executive summary and proposed next steps based on Rishi's runs. Thanks to the team for the quick turn.

Executive summary:
- Short-form embeddings: PASS — p95 <50ms at 500 qps on both Hosted and Dedicated.
- Long-form embeddings: expected headroom issues; Dedicated meets p95 ~175ms at ~320 qps but does not reach 500 qps. Recommend separate pool.
- Reranker: Dedicated passes the SLA for candidate sets up to 10 at 100 concurrency (p95=130ms). For candidate set 25 the p95 is marginal (210ms); Hosted is above SLA for the larger candidate sets.

Proposed immediate MAP updates (dates):
- 2026-06-18: Decision call to confirm pilot config (Dedicated pool + KV cache enabled / separate long-embeddings pool).
- 2026-06-20: If go, provisioning of Dedicated pool (2x reranker workers) and test verification run.
- 2026-06-24: Pilot kickoff (sign-off, procurement steps initiated).

Open asks for SearchCorp before the decision call:
1) Confirm target candidate set distribution for pilot (we assume 70% @10 candidates, 20% @3, 10% @25).
2) Confirm willingness to run the pilot on Dedicated (we provided cost delta in the attachment).

Next steps from Redwood: Rishi can re-run with sharded reranker if you want a comfort run — requires ~24hrs. I'll set up the decision call for 2026-06-18 at 10:00am PT unless you request otherwise.

Best,
Monica
